summary: How Iridium, COSPAS-SARSAT, Inmarsat and GPS work: their orbits, frequencies, services and antennas.

blocks.title: Why satellites
items: Satellite: a radio relay high above the Earth, reaching stations hidden by the Earth's curve.
Orbit: the lower the satellite, the faster it goes. At one height above the equator a trip takes 1 day, so it seems to hang still: geostationary.

blocks.title: Iridium
items: Iridium is a satellite telephone network. Low orbit lets small handheld phones reach it.
Band: 1616 to 1626 MHz for telephone and messaging.
Service: digital voice and data at 2.4 kbps. No analog voice.
Spot beams: for the exam, 48 per satellite, with a footprint of 30 miles in diameter. Each is really about 250 miles across.
Constellation: 66 active satellites in 6 planes.

blocks.title: Beacon search
items: Main job: monitor 406 MHz for distress calls from EPIRBs and relay them to ground stations, the local user terminals.
Position: measured from the Doppler shift of the 406 MHz signal at several points in the orbit.

blocks.title: Inmarsat
items: Coverage: geostationary satellites reach vessels in nearly all the world's navigable waters, but not the polar regions.

head: Service
Carries
Antenna
rows: Voice 16, fax 14.4, data 64/54 kbps, real time
Routine and distress text, store-and-forward, no voice

blocks.title: Inmarsat details
items: Store-and-forward: the land earth station stores the whole message, then forwards it.
High-speed data, 64/54 kbps: B, M4 and Fleet. Fast data needs high gain, so a directional antenna.
Inmarsat-B needs a clear line of sight. A mast on a certain course, a satellite on a low elevation, or going beyond its effective radius can each stop it.

blocks.title: GPS
items: GPS, Global Positioning System: each satellite broadcasts its exact time and position. Travel time gives distance.
Constellation: 24 satellites normally in operation, 4 in each of 6 equally spaced orbital planes.
Frequencies: 1227.6 MHz and 1575.4 MHz.
4 satellites give complete position and time. 4 unknowns: latitude, longitude, altitude, receiver clock error.
DGPS, Differential GPS: a surveyed reference station broadcasts correction factors to improve position accuracy.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Iridium isn't 48 satellites in 4 planes, 55° or 85 minutes.
121.5 MHz is an older beacon frequency. Satellites listen on 406.
1 satellite's pass is enough. Only beacons with built-in GPS send their own position.
Inmarsat isn't polar, or truly global.
Inmarsat-C is omnidirectional. It isn't real time, voice or worldwide.
GPS isn't polar or geosynchronous. Don't confuse 1226.6 with 1227.6.
DGPS: D is differential, not digital. Corrections don't come from the GPS satellites.
